threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to queue for a bus like it’s a ride at Alton Towers. Here, it’s all about the dash and grab.
Caught a late 196 last night. A guy in a parka kept shouting about how his mum's curry beats all takeaways. Brixton never sleeps, even at 2 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler in pigtails taking a dog for a walk while their parent shouted in three languages from the balcony. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble upon a currywurst stand at 3 AM, where locals argue over the best sauce. It’s a delicious debate!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know to avoid the Civic Center BART on Fridays—loud bangs and smoke make it a great excuse to take a bus instead.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, caught a Muni with a broken bell that just kept dinging every block. The driver was grinning, but the rest of us were gritting our teeth.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think Gràcia is all about Gaudí. They miss the quiet plazas where locals sip vermut on a Sunday afternoon, enjoying the real vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at the metro map, trying to figure out the R1 while holding a café con leche like it’s a trophy.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always tell the newcomers; they still think Dalston's just a place with cafes, not an underground music hub where every night is a surprise.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with 90s R&B. Only in Brixton would people actually join in instead of shushing him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the bakery on Weserstraße and catching the scent of fresh bread mixed with the sound of a street musician playing an old folk tune. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you see guys setting up a full bar on the sidewalk for a spontaneous party, complete with disco lights and homemade cocktails.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to BART delays; the eye roll is universal. Newcomers still look at their phones like there's a solution.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a Muni bus driver calmly pulled over mid-route to help a lost tourist read the map. Classic SF kindness in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Sagrada Família is the heart of Barcelona. Try finding a local in Gràcia who doesn't prefer a pint on a quiet terrace instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot a recent arrival by their confusion when the metro goes on strike, checking their phones for train times like it’s a lifeline.
